Photo: Rijksmuseum/Kelly Schenk. AMSTERDAM .- The Van Eeghen family has donated an extremely rare early 17th-century drawing book to the Rijksmuseum. It had been in the family’s possession for more than three centuries, carefully kept and passed down from generation to generation. All the while, it was unknown which artists had created the spectacular drawings inside the book, until around 20 years ago, when a link was established between the book and the work of Rombout Uylenburgh and his workshop. Uylenburgh was a painter from the northern Dutch province of Friesland who worked at the Polish royal court in Kraków. It is exceptionally rare for a 17th-century drawing book to have survived completely intact. The Van Eeghen Drawing Book can be considered a new highlight of the Rijksmuseum Print Room Collection, as well as one of the most significant additions to this collection in recent years. "A substantial part of Rombout Uylenburgh’s small surviving body of work is brought together in a display that will be on view at the Rijksmuseum from 19 August 2026." -- Taco Dibbits, General Director Rijksmuseum The Van Eeghen Drawing Book is a highlight of Dutch draughtsmanship. The donation enables the Rijksmuseum to introduce everyone to Rombout Uylenburgh, a fascinating artist of whom very little work has survived. We are extremely grateful to the Van Eeghen family for this generous gift, which is in keeping with a long-standing family tradition. The Van Eeghen Drawing Book The exceptional Van Eeghen Drawing Book contains some 30 drawings, including a beautifully executed series of biblical scenes attributed to Rombout Uylenburgh and his workshop. These spectacular, full-page drawings are masterpieces filled with drama and emotion, with some executed on blue paper. As the drawings have scarcely been exposed to light, the colours are still as striking as they were 400 years ago. The words Konstboeck voor Reyer Claessoon (‘Art book for Reyer Claessoon’) appear in gold lettering on the binding. Reyer Claessoon was a merchant from Enkhuizen who, like more of his compatriots, had settled in the Polish port city of Danzig, present-day Gdańsk. He probably knew Rombout Uylenburgh well, as they both were adherents of the Mennonite faith. The same is true of the Van Eeghen family, who acquired the book more than three centuries ago. The drawing book has been on public display only once before, in 1935. Rombout Uylenburgh Rombout Uylenburgh (1580/85–1627/28) was an established and celebrated artist in his own time. Today, however, only a handful of works by him survive. At a young age, he moved with his family from Leeuwarden in the Netherlands to the Polish city of Kraków, where King Sigismund III held court. He went on to become a court painter, while his brother Hendrick also entered the king’s service as a commercial agent, in which capacity he purchased paintings for the royal collections. In 1612, Rombout settled in Danzig, where a Dutch community lived. Here, he probably met Reyer Claessoon. He continued his career successfully, one of his specialities being grisailles, paintings executed entirely in shades of grey. Following his death in Danzig in 1627–28, Rombout gradually fell into obscurity. His family, however, became increasingly well known. His brother Hendrick returned from Poland, settled in Amsterdam and became Rembrandt’s art dealer. In 1634, Rembrandt married Saskia van Uylenburgh, a cousin of Rombout and Hendrick. Research and display For a long time, it was unclear which artists had worked in the drawing book, until the previous owner, C.P. van Eeghen (1921-2014), noticed a connection between a sheet by Rombout Uylenburgh in the Rijksmuseum collection and one in his book. This attribution was first published in 2013 by the late Erik Löffler, curator at the Netherlands Institute for Art History (RKD). That publication led to the discovery of a series of paintings by Rombout Uylenburgh in the collection of Museum Ons’ Lieve Heer op Solder in Amsterdam. This gift enables the Rijksmuseum to conduct further research into the work of Rombout Uylenburgh. Besides a small number of paintings, only two drawings by him are known to have survived, one of which is in the collection of the Rijksmuseum. Thanks to a loan from the Rembrandt House Museum, an important part of his surviving work will be brought together for the first time in the display at the Rijksmuseum, on view from 19 August 2026. https://nineoclock.ro/bucharest-stock-ex.text: ABOUT US NINE O’CLOCK STAFF 2024 COMMERCIAL OFFER – 2026 Subscribe to the Nine O’Clock 2026 CONTACT Special price offer 2026 with a 50% discount Bucharest Stock Exchange Receives ASF Approval for the New Multilateral Trading System Code and Launches a New Stage of Capital Market Development by Creating the SME Growth Market 29 August 2026 / By Mihai Manea , Publisher of N ine O’Clock The Bucharest Stock Exchange (BVB) announces that the Financial Supervisory Authority (ASF) has approved the new Multilateral Trading System (MTS) Code. This modern regulatory framework redefines the market architecture and creates the SME Growth Market, a new segment dedicated to companies in their expansion and acceleration phase. The new Code represents one of the most significant modernizations of the Multilateral Trading System in recent years. It aligns the market operated by BVB with European models designed for small and medium-sized enterprise financing through a clearer, more rigorous, and growth-oriented framework. The operational launch of the SME Growth Market will take place following the completion of the necessary technical and operational steps. Remus Vulpescu, CEO of the Bucharest Stock Exchange. “The new Multilateral Trading System Code marks a strategic step forward in the development of the Romanian capital market. By creating the SME Growth Market, we offer SMEs – the backbone of the Romanian economy – and high-potential companies a clear pathway toward funding, visibility, and maturity, while providing investors with a framework built on transparency, corporate governance, and high-quality standards. Aligning the Bucharest Stock Exchange with the European SME Growth Markets community reconfirms our commitment to building a modern, competitive capital market connected to international best practices, ” said Remus Vulpescu, CEO of the Bucharest Stock Exchange. A New Architecture for the MTS The new Code organizes the Multilateral Trading System into three distinct markets: SME Growth Market – dedicated to expanding companies; Base Market (AeRO Market) – intended for issuers not included in the Growth Market; International MTS – dedicated to financial instruments admitted to trading on regulated markets or equivalent MTSs from other jurisdictions. A New Model for Corporate Financing The SME Growth Market introduces a modern admission and monitoring framework built around issuer quality and investor trust, incorporating the following elements: Scoring model for admission; Strong focus on corporate governance; Enhanced financial transparency; Continuous monitoring of issuers; An expanded role for the Authorized Advisor. Companies will be able to raise capital through equity or bond issues, via public offerings as well as private placements, leveraging a platform specifically designed to support their growth and prepare them for a future transfer to the Main Market. Issuer classification on the SME Growth Market will be carried out based on a scoring model outlined in the Code, which evaluates both mandatory requirements and additional criteria such as corporate governance, transparency, and organizational maturity. Alignment with European Standards The Code update is part of BVB’s strategy to modernize the local capital market and aligns with European best practices for SME-dedicated markets, offering entrepreneurs a more competitive financing mechanism and investors a framework with higher standards of transparency, discipline, and monitoring. By creating the SME Growth Market, BVB aligns itself with the latest European practices. The Growth Market will benefit from a dedicated benchmark index, initially comprising the most representative issuers on the AeRO Market that opt for reclassification to the Growth Market and meet the applicable eligibility criteria. The index may subsequently serve as the basis for the development of investment products designed to track its performance, including exchange-traded funds (ETFs). Entry into Force The effective date of the new Multilateral Trading System Code and the launch date of the SME Growth Market will be announced at a later stage. https://www.euronews.com/my-europe/2026/.text: Prosecutors in Poland have launched a terrorism investigation into a fire at a drone factory in the city of Skarżysko-Kamienna.In a statement, prosecutors said the fire, which broke out at a WB Electronics factory, was started deliberately "by planting an explosive device containing flammable materials."CCTV footage had reportedly captured an unidentified person in a balaclava who allegedly entered the premises after climbing a fence. A backpack and a sweatshirt were also found near the site.WB Electronics is the largest private arms company in Poland. Its reconnaissance and attack drones are used by the Ukrainian armed forces.Prosecutors said in their statement that an investigation had been launched into "participation in the activities of a foreign intelligence service against the Republic of Poland and the commission of a terrorist offense, consisting of the deliberate setting of a fire on August 31, 2026, on the premises of WB Electronics S.A. in Skarżysko-Kamienna."It added: "As a result of the fire, warehouse facilities were destroyed, and the value of the damage caused amounts to at least 15 million PLN."InvestigationThe local fire service said the fire at the facility "was not large" and that firefighters took just under two hours to tackle it.After the blaze had been put out, police officers secured the scene and began a detailed investigation.A fire investigation expert is also working at the scene.WB Group respondsThe plant in Skarżysko-Kamienna produces components for unmanned systems destined for the Polish army.Remigiusz Wilk of WB Group told TVN24 that the company has enjoyed the trust of the Polish military and other armies for years."We are, in a sense, part of Poland's security system as a major entity that cooperates with thousands of enterprises across the country – from very small firms to giants such as the Polish Armaments Group, which is a subcontractor in some of our projects," Wilk said."When it comes to unmanned systems worldwide, we are one of the largest manufacturers. These are not single platforms; they are systems linked together into one large 'ecosystem,'" he said.Speaking about the fire, Wilk said the facility would be ready to resume production as soon as authorities completed their work. He added that he did not expect the incident to cause delays in deliveries to the Polish armed forces.Second similar fire within 24 hoursThe incident marked the second similar fire in 24 hours.On Sunday, firefighters were called to a blaze at a warehouse in Lublin belonging to a company that produces aircraft parts.Asked about a possible link between the two incidents, Karolina Galecka, a spokeswoman for the Polish Ministry of the Interior and Administration, said authorities would investigate every possible lead.British newspaper "The Telegraph," citing western intelligence sources, recently reported on a series of suspected Russian sabotage operations in Europe targeting arms factories and companies supplying weapons to Ukraine.According to those reports, the operations are being carried out in a way designed to stay below the threshold that could trigger NATO's Article 5, which commits allies to collective defence should one of them come under attack.

Photograph: Reuters Capital punishment Texas kills man by lethal injection in state’s fifth execution this year LeJames Norman, 40, killed at Huntsville penitentiary while scheduled execution in Georgia halted by judge Associated Press Wed 16 Sep 2026 20.13 EDT First published on Wed 16 Sep 2026 08.32 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A man convicted over the shooting deaths of three people was executed on Wednesday in Texas, while another execution scheduled for the same time in Georgia was halted by a judge. It’s the fifth execution in Texas this year. Georgia has yet to put anyone to death this year. The nation’s busiest death chamber is in Florida, which accounted for more than half the 25 executions already carried out in the US this year. LeJames Norman, 40, was sentenced to death over the 2005 deaths of Samuel Roberts, 24, Tiffani Peacock, 18, and Celso Lopez, 38, inside the home they shared in a small, rural town. He died by injection of the sedative pentobarbital at the state penitentiary in Huntsville, Texas. Stacey Humphreys, 53, was convicted of malice murder and other crimes in the 2003 killings of 33-year-old Cyndi Williams and 21-year-old Lori Brown. He had been scheduled to die at 7pm ET at the state prison near Jackson in Georgia. However, a judge halted Humphreys’ execution late on Tuesday after his lawyers filed a petition seeking a resentencing under a new state law that allows victims of abuse to have their sentences reconsidered and reduced, if they can tie their crimes to abuse they suffered. The state appealed against that ruling, asking the Georgia supreme court to find that Humphreys was not entitled to have his sentence reconsidered under the new law. But the high court declined to hear that appeal before the scheduled execution time and left the lower court’s stay in place. Norman and Ker’Sean Ramey believed there was cocaine in the house in Edna, a small, rural city about 100 miles (161km) south-west of Houston, and hoped to steal it, according to court records. But they never found any drugs and fatally shot three people in the home. Lopez was shot four times, including three in the back of his head. Peacock was shot twice in the head. Roberts was shot five times to the chest, neck and head. Norman was arrested about five months after the killings while trying to cross back into the US from Mexico. He pleaded guilty to capital murder, leaving a jury to decide his punishment. Ramey was also convicted in the shootings and sentenced to death. His execution is set for next week. The Texas board of pardons and paroles on Monday voted against commuting Norman’s sentence to a lesser penalty or recommending a 90-day reprieve of execution. After the Texas court of criminal appeals on Monday denied a motion from Norman’s attorneys for a stay of execution based on claims regarding actions by the prosecution, his attorneys have asked the US supreme court to review the decision. In 2017, the supreme court refused to review Norman’s appeal that raised questions about the competence of his trial attorneys. The two women Humphreys killed were working as real-estate agents for a new subdivision in the Atlanta suburb of Powder Springs. He entered the sales office in a model home around midday on 3 November 2003, and forced them to strip naked and give him their bank pins before fatally shooting them, according to evidence presented at trial. Humphreys withdrew more than $3,000 from the women’s bank accounts, according to court filings. He told police after his arrest that he had recently taken out some high-interest payday loans and needed money for a payment on his truck. Witnesses told police they saw a man fitting Humphreys’ description at the sales office and a vehicle in the parking lot that matched his black Dodge Durango. Police zeroed in on Humphreys and tried to question him at his Dunwoody home days later. He fled and was arrested in Wisconsin after leading police on a high-speed chase. Humphreys’ lawyers have argued that he should be resentenced because his death sentence was tainted by a biased juror who lied during jury selection and bullied other jurors into voting for a death sentence. Courts have repeatedly rejected those arguments for procedural reasons, though US supreme court justice Sonia Sotomayor, joined by the other two liberal justices, argued last year that the issue should be further explored rather than leaving it “caught in a web of procedural barriers”. Additionally, Humphreys’ lawyers have argued that it was not fair that his clemency application was heard by only four members of the five-person state board of pardons and paroles. A judge had ordered one member of the board to recuse herself, agreeing with Humphreys’ legal team that there was a conflict of interest because she previously worked as a victim advocate with the Cobb county district attorney’s office and had worked with the victims in his case. The parole board on Tuesday denied clemency for Humphreys.
